sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Historian Nini Rodgers died at the age of 86. Throughout a four-decade career at Queen’s University Belfast, she taught thousands of students and championed part-time night degrees. In 2007, she published her major work, Ireland, Slavery and Anti-Slavery: 1612-1865, challenging Ireland's self-image regarding the transatlantic slave trade. She was the daughter of Marie and the poet WR Rodgers, and partner to the late historian Jack Gray.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Rodgers's research meticulously unmasked the reality of Ireland's involvement in slavery, replacing comforting fables with precise knowledge. She also shaped generations of historians and brought higher education to new kinds of people through her commitment to part-time students.

Haines remains in critical condition while police allege the incident was targeted.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: An independent politician was struck by a car in Victoria on Monday and remains in critical condition following surgery. A local man was charged with several offences, including causing serious injury and harming a public official, and is scheduled to appear in court.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Police stated they will allege the vehicle strike was targeted. The suspect's father and partner released a statement expressing shock and noting a long friendship with the politician, while the local community held a vigil.
